checks.statement: Aff(1,F2), Aff(Z2), and S2 have the displayed order-2 identification; A2 is trivial.
checks.reasoning: In F2 the only nonzero multiplier is 1, so x maps to x+b gives exactly two affine permutations. An automorphism of the additive group Z2 fixes its unique nonidentity element, leaving the same two translations. The two permutations of a two-element set contain only the identity as an even permutation.
checks.outcome: The displayed claims are consistent under the usual meanings of these symbols.

checks.statement: The groups Aff(1,F3) and Gl(2,F2) each identify with the permutations of a three-element set.
checks.reasoning: Aff(1,F3) has 3 choices of translation and 2 nonzero multipliers, giving 6 distinct permutations of F3. In dimension 2 over F2 an ordered basis has 3 choices of first nonzero vector and 2 choices outside its span, giving 6 invertible matrices; their action on the 3 nonzero vectors is faithful. Each action therefore exhausts S3.
checks.outcome: The order and action checks support the displayed comparison chain without deciding any uncertain handwriting.

checks.statement: F3-plus is cyclic of order 3, F3-star is cyclic of order 2, and the F2-star quotient does not change Gl(2,F2).
checks.reasoning: Addition modulo 3 cycles through 0,1,2. The nonzero residues modulo 3 are 1 and 2, with 2 squared equal to 1. The only nonzero residue in F2 is 1, so the scalar subgroup in the displayed quotient is trivial. The even permutations on three letters are the identity and the two 3-cycles, hence form a cyclic order-3 group.
checks.outcome: The lower group identifications and final A3 statement are consistent. This does not choose rotated simeq versus equals or an alphabet for A.

checks.statement: One-dimensional vector spaces over F2 have a unique linear isomorphism between them.
checks.reasoning: Each such space has exactly one nonzero vector. A linear isomorphism must send that vector to the sole nonzero vector of the target, and this assignment is linear and bijective.
checks.outcome: The written can. isomorphes claim is verified for the stated field and dimension.
